54366-a-colonial-reformer-vol-3-of-3.creator: Rolf Boldrewood
54366-a-colonial-reformer-vol-3-of-3.description: A book by Rolf Boldrewood. Deriving his leading characteristics from Nature’s gift—very scantily supplemented by education—he yet possessed the rare qualities of apprehensive acuteness, intrepidity, and discrimination in such measure and proportion as a hundred prize-takers at competitive examinations might have vainly hoped to emulate.

arxiv-2205-03980.title: Dynamical and qKZ equations modulo p s p^{s} , an example
arxiv-2205-03980.creator: Alexander Varchenko
arxiv-2205-03980.description: Abstract . We consider an example of the joint system of dynamical differential equations and qKZ difference equations with parameters corresponding to equations for elliptic integrals. We solve this system of equations modulo any power p n p^{n} of a prime integer p p .

arxiv-2209-10856.title: A nice two-loop next-to-next-to-MHV amplitude in 𝒩 = 4 {\cal N}=4 super-Yang-Mills
arxiv-2209-10856.creator: Song He, Zhenjie Li, Chi Zhang
arxiv-2209-10856.description: Abstract We study a scalar component of the 8-point next-to-next-to-maximally-helicity-violating (N 2 MHV) amplitude at two-loop level in 𝒩 = 4 {\cal N}=4 super-Yang-Mills theory; it has a leading singularity proportional to the inverse of the four-mass-box square root and receives contributions from only two types of non-trivial integrals with one-loop infrared (IR) divergences.

The research

arxiv-2302-00231.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A. Defant, D. Galicer, M. Mansilla, M. Mastyło, S. Muro. arxiv-2408-01303.title: A Systematic Mapping Study on SDN Controllers for Enhancing Security in IoT Networks
arxiv-2408-01303.creator: Charles Oredola, Adnan Ashraf
arxiv-2408-01303.description: Abstract Context: The increase in Internet of Things (IoT) devices gives rise to an increase in deceptive manipulations by malicious actors. These actors should be prevented from targeting the IoT networks. Cybersecurity threats have evolved and become dynamically sophisticated, such that they could exploit any vulnerability found in IoT networks.

arxiv-2408-02328.title: Past and future of the cap set problem
arxiv-2408-02328.creator: Ernie Croot, Vsevolod F. Lev, Péter Pál Pach
arxiv-2408-02328.description: Abstract 1. Roth’s problem on three-term progressions In 1953 K. F. Roth [ 37 ] proved that the largest subset of [N]:=\{1,2,...,N\} containing no three-term arithmetic progression x,x+d,x+2d has size o(N) . Working through his proof (suitably interpreted) one can even get a quantitative bound of the form O(N/\log\log N) . This then naturally leads to the following question.

arxiv-2410-11055.title: Varying Shades of Wrong: Aligning LLMs with Wrong Answers Only
arxiv-2410-11055.creator: Jihan Yao Wenxuan Ding Shangbin Feng Lucy Lu Wang Yulia Tsvetkov
arxiv-2410-11055.description: Abstract In the absence of abundant reliable annotations for challenging tasks and contexts, how can we expand the frontier of LLM capabilities with potentially wrong answers? We focus on two research questions: (1) Can LLMs generate reliable preferences among wrong options? And if so, (2) Would alignment with such wrong-over-wrong preferences be helpful?

arxiv-2410-16429.title: Pantograph: A Machine-to-Machine Interaction Interface for Advanced Theorem Proving, High Level Reasoning, and Data Extraction in Lean 4
arxiv-2410-16429.creator: Leni Aniva Chuyue Sun Brando Miranda Clark Barrett Sanmi Koyejo, {aniva,chuyues,brando90,barrettc,sanmi}@stanford.edu
arxiv-2410-16429.description: Abstract Machine-assisted theorem proving refers to the process of conducting structured reasoning to automatically generate proofs for mathematical theorems. Recently, there has been a surge of interest in using machine learning models in conjunction with proof assistants to perform this task.

arxiv-2411-00041.title: NeuroSym-BioCAT: Leveraging Neuro-Symbolic Methods for Biomedical Scholarly Document Categorization and Question Answering
arxiv-2411-00041.creator: Parvez Zamil, Gollam Rabby, Md. Sadekur Rahman, Sören Auer
arxiv-2411-00041.description: Abstract The growing volume of biomedical scholarly document abstracts presents an increasing challenge in efficiently retrieving accurate and relevant information. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that integrates an optimized topic modelling framework, OVB-LDA, with the BI-POP CMA-ES optimization technique for enhanced scholarly document abstract categorization.

arxiv-2506-18557.title: Object-aware Sound Source Localization via Audio-Visual Scene Understanding
arxiv-2506-18557.creator: Sung Jin Um, Dongjin Kim, Sangmin Lee, Jung Uk Kim
arxiv-2506-18557.description: Abstract Audio-visual sound source localization task aims to spatially localize sound-making objects within visual scenes by integrating visual and audio cues. However, existing methods struggle with accurately localizing sound-making objects in complex scenes, particularly when visually similar silent objects coexist.

arxiv-2510-15803.title: Dynamic Recalibration in LiDAR SLAM: Integrating AI and Geometric Methods with Real-Time Feedback Using INAF Fusion*
arxiv-2510-15803.creator: Zahra Arjmandi, Gunho Sohn
arxiv-2510-15803.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel fusion technique for LiDAR Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), aimed at improving localization and 3D mapping using LiDAR sensor. Our approach centers on the Inferred Attention Fusion (INAF) module, which integrates AI with geometric odometry.

plos-pone-0009848.title: Clinical Utility of a Commercial LAM-ELISA Assay for TB Diagnosis in HIV-Infected Patients Using Urine and Sputum Samples
plos-pone-0009848.creator: Keertan Dheda, Virginia Davids, Laura Lenders et al.
plos-pone-0009848.description: PLOS ONE research article. The accurate diagnosis of TB in HIV-infected patients, particularly with advanced immunosuppression, is difficult. Recent studies indicate that a lipoarabinomannan (LAM) assay (Clearview-TB®-ELISA) may have some utility for the diagnosis of TB in HIV-infected patients; however, t

pmc-11401346.title: The association between macrosomia and glucose, lipids and hormones levels in maternal and cord serum: a case-control study
pmc-11401346.creator: Xinxin Xing, Yifan Duan, Jie Wang, Zhenyu Yang, Qingqing Man, Jianqiang Lai
pmc-11401346.description: BackgroundThe formation of macrosomia is associated with excessive nutrition and/or unable to regulate effectively. This case-control study aims to explore the relationship between macrosomia and glucose, lipids and hormones levels in maternal and cord serum.MethodsIn the case-control study, 78 pairs of mothers and newborns were recruited who received care at one hospital of Hebei, China between 2016 and 2019.

pmc-11509389.title: Therapeutic Effect of Decellularized Extracellular Matrix from Fish Skin for Accelerating Skin Regeneration
pmc-11509389.creator: Seong-Yeong Heo, Tae-Hee Kim, Se-Chang Kim, Gun-Woo Oh, Soo-Jin Heo, Won-Kyo Jung
pmc-11509389.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A cellular matrix derived from natural tissue functions as a highly biocompatible and versatile material for wound healing application. It provides a complex and highly organized environment with biological molecules and physical stimuli. Recently, various kinds of tissue/organ decellularized extracellular matrixes (dECMs) from bovine and porcine have been used as biomedical applications to support tissue regeneration but inherit religious restrictions and the risk of disease transmission to humans.

pmc-11805250.title: To Evaluate and Compare the Microleakage of Chitosan Nano Hydrogel-Incorporated MTA and Glass Ionomer Cements When used as a Retrograde Filling Material
pmc-11805250.creator: Vinaykumar G. Suryavanshi, Ravi K. Tale, Vivekanand D. Kolvekar, Rashmi Chordiya, P S Amal, B Abijeet
pmc-11805250.description: Background:An inadequate apical seal stands out as a primary cause of disappointment in surgical endodontic procedures. Therefore, the choice of root-end filling material should aim to prevent the leakage of potential contaminants into the periapical tissue.Aim:To evaluate and compare microleakage of chitosan nano hydrogel-incorporated mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) and glass ionomer cement (GIC) when used as a retrograde filling material.

pmc-12565861.title: DPAGT1—Perspective as an Anticancer Drug Target
pmc-12565861.creator: Michio Kurosu, Katsuhiko Mitachi
pmc-12565861.description: Tunicamycins trigger endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress by inhibiting DPAGT1 (dolichyl-phosphate N-acetylglucosamine-phosphotransferase 1): the rate-limiting enzyme that initiates N-glycan biosynthesis. Aberrant N-glycan branching is a hallmark of many solid tumors, and distinct cancer-associated N-glycan structures have been identified. Evidence shows that tunicamycins suppress key oncogenic processes, including proliferation, apoptosis resistance, metastasis, and angiogenesis.

pmc-12702796.title: From sick care to healthspan: educating the longevity physician for health maintenance and health promotion
pmc-12702796.creator: Dominik Thor, David Barzilai, Yu-Xuan Lyu, Luiza Spiru
pmc-12702796.description: This paper focuses specifically on the education and upskilling of medical doctors, proposing how longevity-related competencies can be incorporated first through continuing medical education (CME) pathways and, eventually, into formal medical curricula. As longevity medicine evolves from research into clinical practice, education has emerged as its defining challenge.

pmc-12719851.title: First evaluation of a novel pulsatile LVAD: Feasibility and haemodynamic impact in acute heart failure
pmc-12719851.creator: Sara Knigge, Marcelo B. Bastos, Bastian Schmack, Liam Schana, Oren Malchin, Ali S. Merzah, Aron F. Popov, Alexander Weymann, Arjang Ruhparwar, Felix Schumacher, Günes Dogan, Jan D. Schmitto
pmc-12719851.description: AimsNon‐pharmacological therapies for acute decompensated heart failure (HF) and cardiogenic shock have evolved considerably in recent decades. Short‐term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices can be used as circulatory backup. While nearly all available devices use continuous flow, evidence indicates that pulsatile flow can be more effective.

pmc-13084862.title: RNA helicase SKIV2L impedes tumor immunity by reprogramming arginine metabolism of hepatocellular carcinomas
pmc-13084862.creator: Lisheng Zhu, Meng Wu, Bingbing Feng, Yu Zhang, Yang Xu, Lili Yu
pmc-13084862.description: Background and aimsHuman solid tumors such as hepatocellular carcinomas (HCC) establish a complex immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that undermines the efficacy of existing immunotherapies such as chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR T) cell therapy. To advance immunotherapy for HCC, it is crucial to delineate the molecular mechanisms that drive TME formation and immune evasion.

pmc-13114499.title: Silver‐enhanced Photoresponsive g‐C3N4/Ag Janus Microrobots With Negative Photogravitaxis Efficient Antibiotic Degradation
pmc-13114499.creator: Yunhuan Yuan, Vinicius Tadeu Santana, Stanisław Wacławek, Michal Mazur, Martin Pumera
pmc-13114499.description: Water pollution remains a serious global challenge; hence, the efficient, low‐cost, and environmentally friendly removal of pollutants from water has become a research hotspot. Photocatalytic microrobots can achieve autonomous movement and generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), presenting a great opportunity for water purification.

pmc-13262741.title: Exploring the diversity of leafhoppers (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) in the Eastern Canadian Arctic
pmc-13262741.creator: Abraão Almeida Santos, Nicolas Plante, Sarah Parceaud-May, Jordanne Jacques, Amélie Grégoire-Taillefer, Edel Pérez-López, Brian Bahder
pmc-13262741.description: The diversity of leafhoppers (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) in the Arctic is likely underestimated, limiting the ability to document community changes due to uncertainty in species occurrence and a lack of long-term monitoring data. The Nunavik Sentinels community science program documents pollinator diversity across the Boreal, Subarctic, and Arctic regions of Québec (Eeyou Istchee and Nunavik) and Newfoundland and Labrador (Nunatsiavut).

pmc-13416726.title: Benefits of Incobotulinumtoxin A in Pain, Spasticity and Functionality—A 5 Years Review
pmc-13416726.creator: André Cruz
pmc-13416726.description: Introduction: Pain is a major contributor to functional impairment in neurological patients. Botulinum toxin type A (BT-A) is well-established for focal spasticity and has shown some benefits in pain reduction. Long-term data from large cohorts remain limited. Material and Methods: This retrospective study (2017–2022) analyzed 20 variables from spastic patients treated with Incobotulinumtoxin A (INCO) for pain and spasticity.

pmc-13518064.title: ERICA-trio: an outgroup-free deep learning method for topology inference and introgression detection
pmc-13518064.creator: Yubo Zhang, Weifan Lv, Wei Zhang
pmc-13518064.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Genetic admixture is a widespread phenomenon across diverse organisms. Conventional algorithms for inferring species relationship and detecting introgression often rely on outgroup data, which can be challenging to obtain and may introduce bias. Given the demonstrated efficacy and flexibility of neural networks in topology inference and introgression detection, we developed a deep learning-based method, ERICA-trio, to reconstruct evolutionary relationships among three taxa without requiring outgroup data.

pmc-13544322.title: A phase III clinical trial of PXT3003 in Chinese patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A
pmc-13544322.creator: Xiaoxuan Liu, Wanqian Cao, Hongli Li, Chen Sun, Jingzheng Hao, Yuwei Da, Baoyu Yuan, Ning Wang, Shan Wu, Jun Liu, Zuneng Lu, Qi Fang, Zhi-Ying Wu, Liying Yuan, Jiaoting Jin, Haishan Jiang, Yaling Liu, Mingming Ma, Ling Wei, Jianglong Tu, Xiaoli Yao, Yuan Sun, Xuefan Yu, Yiming Liu, Di Zhong, Yun Xu,
pmc-13544322.description: SummaryCharcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A (CMT1A) is the most common inherited peripheral neuropathy and currently lacks disease-modifying therapy. PXT3003, a low-dose oral combination targeting PMP22 overexpression, has shown efficacy in two trials, while one recent confirmatory trial failed to meet its primary efficacy endpoints.

pmc-13552417.title: Risk Factors and Predictors of Pneumonia Among Under-Five Children in Sana’a City, Yemen: A Multicenter Case-Control Study
pmc-13552417.creator: Mohammed Al-Shehab, Rashad Abdul-Ghani, Muneera Muthana Zaid, Ahmed A Azazy, Sayaf A Alsoofi, Reham S Al-Areqi, Rawan A Al-Akwaa, Mohammed H Al-Arashani, Kafa Alwan Ali Alkhder, Sahar A Thabet, Ahlam Abdulmalik Esmail, Ahmed S Hudna
pmc-13552417.description: BackgroundPneumonia is a major cause of preventable morbidity and mortality among under-five children, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected countries. However, evidence from Yemen remains scarce. This study examined child-related, maternal, and environmental factors possibly associated with pneumonia among under-five children in Sana’a City, Yemen.

uslaw-usc-t18-s647.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s647.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 31 (Embezzlement And Theft). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever knowingly receives, from a clerk or other officer of a court of the United States, as a deposit, loan, or otherwise, any money belonging in the registry of such court, is guilty of embezzlement, and shall be fined under.
